title: Orbital period by altitude (minutes)
notes: The ISS orbits at about 400 km altitude with a period of about 93 minutes (NASA). GPS satellites orbit at about 20,200 km altitude with a roughly 12-hour (720-minute) period. Geostationary satellites orbit at about 35,786 km with a period matching Earth's rotation, 24 hours (1,440 minutes) -- which is why they appear to hover over one spot. Higher altitude means a longer orbital period (Kepler's third law).
